summary.en-US: See X (Twitter) rate limits, reset countdowns and limit errors from the requests your browser already makes. Nothing is sent anywhere.

description.en-US:
Rate Limit Tracker for X shows the rate limits X (formerly Twitter) applies to your account, using the requests your browser already makes. No extra requests, no account connection, nothing sent anywhere.

**What you get**

- Remaining requests and reset countdowns for follows, unfollows, posts and likes
- Limit hits caught even when X doesn't return a 429, such as a follow limit reported as an error code
- Every X API endpoint that reports a rate limit, sorted by how close it is to running out
- A request log you can filter to tracked actions or errors
- A toolbar badge with the lowest remaining count, which turns red after you hit a limit

**Make it yours**

- Choose which actions to track and which appear on the home screen
- Track any other X endpoint by name, path or URL, or with one click from the Endpoints page
- Export your history as JSON, or clear it at any time

**Private by design**

- Runs only on x.com
- Never reads cookies, tokens or request headers
- Keeps only rate-limit headers, status codes and X's error codes
- All data stays on your device, with no servers, analytics or tracking
- Open source under the MIT license: https://github.com/toneflix/x-ratelimit

**First run:** Firefox asks you to allow access to x.com. Open the extension's popup and click **Grant x.com access**.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by X Corp.

version.approval_notes:
Source code: the uploaded source archive is the git tree of the release commit (also public at https://github.com/toneflix/x-ratelimit). The extension is written in TypeScript and bundled with tsdown (Rolldown). The output is not minified, and builds are deterministic.

To reproduce the submitted package:
1. Install Node.js 24 (built with 24.22.0) and npm 11.
2. Unzip the source archive and cd into it.
3. npm ci
4. npm run build:firefox
The output in dist/firefox/ is identical to the submitted package.

What it does:
- background.js observes responses from https://x.com/i/api/* with webRequest.onHeadersReceived (read-only, no blocking) and keeps only status codes and rate-limit headers.
- content.js runs on x.com and injects hook.js (a packaged web_accessible_resource) into the page. hook.js wraps fetch/XMLHttpRequest to observe responses, never requests, and reports status, rate-limit headers and X error codes back via postMessage.
- No request headers or cookies are read. Credential-like response headers are dropped.
- No remote code, no network requests of its own. All data stays in storage.local.

To test: install, click Grant x.com access in the popup, browse x.com (for example like a post), then open the popup.
